To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a high‐fat diet does not affect amniotic fluid volumes or amnion aquaglyceroporin gene expression.
high‐fat diet without development of obesity did not affect amnionic fluid volume or aquaporin expression.

(1) AQP1, 3, 8, 9, and 11 are present in amnion of Japanese macaque; (2) AQP1 is highest and AQP 8 lowest in reflected and AQP3, 9, 11 are similar in reflected and non‐reflected amnion; (3) AQP11 mRNA level is positively correlated with AFV in Japanese macaques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of high fat diet on amniotic volume and amnionic aquaporin expression.
the effects of maternal diet on amniotic fluids.
the effects of maternal high‐fat diet and associated high lipid exposure on fetal growth and development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HFD without development obesity does not significantly alter amniotic volume and AQP expression in the non‐obese pregnant Japanese macaques.
HFD in the non‐obese does not have a significant impact on AFV and amnion AQPs.
the HFD in pregnant Japanese macaques does not alter AFV and amnion AQPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HFD without development obesity does not affect amnion AFI and AQP expression in the non‐obese pregnant macaque.
HFD may not have substantial effects on AFV and amnion AQPs in non‐obese pregnant macaques.
the HFD in pregnant Japanese macaques does not affect the amniotic fluid levels, and amnion AQPs are expressed in a regional manner in the macaque.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the macaque model is a useful tool for studying the mechanisms underlying the effects of HFD on fetal development and that AQP expression in the amnion is a potential marker of AFV in this species.
the AFI is a useful measure of AFV in non‐human primates and that the amnion AFI is positively associated with the amnion expression of AQP11, which may be a novel mechanism for regulating AFV.

AFI and AQP expression are similar between control and non-obese HFD pregnant macaques, suggesting that HFD without obesity may have little or no effect on AFV or amnion AQUAPORIN expression in non-human primates.
